children.value: What do we do when an ODE is not exact? For example,

children.html: −yd⁡ ⁣x+xd⁡ ⁣y=0-y \d{x} + x \d{y} = 0−ydx+xdy=0
P=−yQ=x∂P∂y=−1∂Q∂x=1\begin{align} P &= -y & Q &= x \\ \pp{}{P}{y} &= -1 & \pp{}{Q}{x} &= 1 \end{align}P∂y∂P​​=−y=−1​Q∂x∂Q​​=x=1​​

P=−yx2Q=1x∂P∂y=−1x2∂Q∂x=−1x2\begin{align} P &= -\frac{y}{x^2} & Q &= \frac{1}{x} \\ \pp{}{P}{y} &= -\frac{1}{x^2} & \pp{}{Q}{x} &= -\frac{1}{x}^2 \end{align}P∂y∂P​​=−x2y​=−x21​​Q∂x∂Q​​=x1​=−x1​2​​

children.html: y′=x4+y2xy\displaystyle y' = \frac{x^4 + y^2}{xy}y′=xyx4+y2​

children.value: This ODE is not in the standard form, so we need to first rearrange:

children.html: xyd⁡ ⁣y=(x4+y2)d⁡ ⁣x(x4+y2)d⁡ ⁣x−xyd⁡ ⁣y=0\begin{align} xy \d{y} = (x^4+y^2) \d{x} \\ (x^4 + y^2) \d{x} - xy \d{y} = 0 \end{align}xydy=(x4+y2)dx(x4+y2)dx−xydy=0​​
P=x4+y2Q=−xy\begin{align} P &= x^4 + y^2 \\ Q &= -xy \end{align}PQ​=x4+y2=−xy​​

children.value: Check to see if the ODE is exact:

children.html: (∂P∂y)x=2y(∂Q∂x)y=−y\begin{align} \td{}{P}{y}{x} &= 2y \\ \td{}{Q}{x}{y} &= -y \end{align}(∂y∂P​)x​(∂x∂Q​)y​​=2y=−y​​

children.value:
The two partial derivatives are not equal, so the ODE is not exact. In
order to make it exact, we need to find an integrating factor

children.html: R=1Q[(∂P∂y)x−(∂Q∂x)y]=1−xy(2y−(−y))=−3x\begin{align} R &= \frac{1}{Q}\left[\td{}{P}{y}{x} - \td{}{Q}{x}{y} \right] \\ &=\frac{1}{-xy}(2y-(-y)) \\ &= -\frac{3}{x} \end{align}R​=Q1​[(∂y∂P​)x​−(∂x∂Q​)y​]=−xy1​(2y−(−y))=−x3​​​
F=exp⁡(∫−3xd⁡ ⁣x)=e−3ln⁡(x)=x−3F = \exp\left(\int \frac{-3}{x} \d{x}\right) = e^{-3\ln(x)} = x^{-3}F=exp(∫x−3​dx)=e−3ln(x)=x−3

children.value: Apply the integrating factor to the original ODE:

children.html: x−3(x4+y2)d⁡ ⁣x−x−3(xy)d⁡ ⁣y=0(x+y2x−3)d⁡ ⁣x−yx2d⁡ ⁣y=0\begin{align} x^{-3}(x^4+y^2) \d{x} - x^{-3}(xy) \d{y} &= 0 \\ \left(x+\frac{y^2}{x^{-3}}\right) \d{x} - \frac{y}{x^2} \d{y} &= 0 \end{align}x−3(x4+y2)dx−x−3(xy)dy(x+x−3y2​)dx−x2y​dy​=0=0​​

(∂f∂x)y=y2x3+k′(x)=P=x+y2x3k′(x)=x\begin{align} \td{}{f}{x}{y} = \frac{y^2}{x^3} + k'(x) &= P = x + \frac{y^2}{x^3} \\ k'(x) &= x \\ \end{align}(∂x∂f​)y​=x3y2​+k′(x)k′(x)​=P=x+x3y2​=x​​

children.html: y′=−ex+y+yeyxey−1\displaystyle y' = -\frac{e^{x+y} + ye^y}{x e^y - 1}y′=−xey−1ex+y+yey​

children.value: This ODE is not in the standard form, so we need to first rearrange:

children.html: (ex+y+yey)d⁡ ⁣x+(xey−1)d⁡ ⁣y=0\begin{align} (e^{x+y} + ye^y) \d{x} + (x e^y - 1) \d{y} = 0 \end{align}(ex+y+yey)dx+(xey−1)dy=0​​
P=ex+y+yeyQ=xey−1\begin{align} P &= e^{x+y} + ye^y \\ Q &= x e^y - 1 \end{align}PQ​=ex+y+yey=xey−1​​

children.value: Check if the differential equation is exact:

children.html: (∂P∂y)x=ex+y+yey+ey(∂Q∂x)y=ey\begin{align} \td{}{P}{y}{x} &= e^{x+y} + y e^y + e^y \\ \td{}{Q}{x}{y} &= e^y \end{align}(∂y∂P​)x​(∂x∂Q​)y​​=ex+y+yey+ey=ey​​

children.value:
These are not equal, so the equation is not exact. To make it exact, find
integrating factor

children.html: R=1Q[(∂P∂y)x−(∂Q∂x)y]=1xey−1(ex+y+yey+ey−ey)=ey(ex+y)xey−1\begin{align} R &= \frac{1}{Q}\left[\td{}{P}{y}{x} - \td{}{Q}{x}{y} \right] \\ &=\frac{1}{x e^y - 1}(e^{x+y} + y e^y + e^y - e^y) \\ &= \frac{e^y(e^x + y)}{x e^y - 1} \end{align}R​=Q1​[(∂y∂P​)x​−(∂x∂Q​)y​]=xey−11​(ex+y+yey+ey−ey)=xey−1ey(ex+y)​​​

children.html: f(x,y)=∫(ex+y)d⁡ ⁣x=ex+xy+k(y)f(x,y) = \int (e^x + y) \d{x} = e^x + xy + k(y)f(x,y)=∫(ex+y)dx=ex+xy+k(y)
